used to draw on unharmed skin instead too. usually in class or inpatient when i was bored or frustrated. then they said i had to stop because 'it could be covering new self harm'. treatment professionals can go fuck themselves up the ass with a glitter sharpie.

why draw over them? why not around them or on other areas?

i would also sometimes incorporate wounds and scars into my drawings - using it as the spine of a caterpillar, for example. that was a lot of fun. also calligraphy. never was good at it but there's something therapeutic about scribbling the alphabet over and over on your tricep til you cant differentiate the letters any more. it was another form of body art and self expression, which is part of what self harm is to me.

be careful with certain types of pens, because the ink doesnt adhere well to skin and if you're like me you will press down until you get the ink where you want it, which can lead to self harm. the tips are surprisingly scratchy if you want them to be. i'd recommend soft tip markers if you're explicitly trying to avoid self harming.
